newsitem.title: INDIA: Philippines says backs India's APEC bid.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says backs India's APEC bid.

text.p: The Philippines on Monday threw its weight behind India's bid to join the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, and urged Indian businessmen to invest in the southeast Asian nation.

"The Philippine government is supporting the Indian government's entry into APEC. We will surely support your decision to enter APEC," Philippine Trade and Industry undersecretary Jose Juliano told a business seminar.
India has sought to join APEC, which currently has a moratorium on new members. Its 18 member-economies from Asia, North America and South America hope to achieve free regional trade by 2020.
Juliano, in New Delhi with a 78-member business delegation, said Indians would find advantages in investing in the Philippines -- a gateway to southeast Asia offering a raft of tax incentives.
Indian businessmen could also exploit low research and development costs in the Philippines, which were far below those in East Asia, Juliano said.
The two Asian nations have pledged to boost bilateral trade to $500 million by the turn of the century. Trade in January to November 1996 totalled $240 million versus $78 million in 1990.
India was given full dialogue status by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) last July. ASEAN groups Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam.
